ops.title: ClaudeSdkBackend isolation parity: seed a fresh config home for isolated runs
ops.description: Follow-up from the v0.10.0 refuter review (accepted-as-documented, not fixed): `ClaudeSdkBackend` with `isolated=True` achieves settings/MCP hermeticity only (`setting_sources=[]`, `strict_mcp_config`) — it does not seed a fresh `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` the way `ClaudeCliBackend.claude_isolation()` does (core `claude_isolation_sources`/`claude_isolation_seed` ops + keychain fallback), so a parent `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and the ambient `.claude.json` state pass through to "isolated" SDK runs. Parity work: reuse the existing isolation host I/O (claude.py) from the SDK backend, passing the seeded dir via `options.env["CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR"]`. Documented in the class docstring and the security-default doc (c84a4810) until then.

ops.text: ClaudeSdkBackend isolated=True seeds a fresh CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR via the shared core isolation ops (keychain fallback included)
a test proves a parent CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR does not leak into an isolated SDK run
